newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks drop 1.41 pct on Q3, economy worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks drop 1.41 pct on Q3, economy worries.

text.p: Thai stocks fell for the fifth consecutive trading day on Tuesday, declining 1.41 percent following sustained selling by foreign investors worried about third quarter earnings and the economy, brokers said.

After dipping below the 900-point mark, the SET index regained some ground in the afternoon and finished 12.96 points lower at 905.34 on 4.6 billion baht trade. It was the lowest close since July 27, 1993, when the index finished at 893.14.
"Foreigners continued selling on persistent concerns over third quarter earnings and the slowing Thai economy," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securities.

Brokers said local mutual funds, which entered the market early last week after Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda asked them to buy to shore up the battered market, bought some stocks today in order to prevent prices from going down too much.
"The SET index might have ended below the 900-point level today if the local mutual funds were idle," said a broker.
The 900-point mark is seen as a strong support level at present, Thanadech said.
Bodi's resignation as finance minister, which became effective today, also caused a slight negative impact on the market, Thanadech said.
Two major sectors gained today while the rest fell. The building and furnishing materials sector rose 1.22 percent while the printing and publishing sector was up 0.25 percent.

In the building and furnishing materials sector, Siam Cement, Thailand's largest cement producer, gained 12 baht to 816 while Siam City Cement rose 10 to 160. Multi media operator the Manager Media Group rose two to 76.

Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling six baht to 69. Thai Military Bank, which raised interest rates on some fixed deposits by up to 50 basis points on Tuesday, lost 3.50 to 59. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
